note: State-owned park run by the Appanoose County Conservation Board, which has its offices and nature center here, on the wooded bluffs above the Chariton River east of Centerville. Six electric sites near the CCC shelter house and playground; pit latrines; water fill and dump at the park entrance. Hiking trails close in January (wildlife refuge). A second entrance leads to a boat ramp. The campground is on the bluff top, back from and above the river. The county gives no pad lengths. --Claude
summary: 30A, 6 sites, pit latrines + fill/dump, open year-round and first-come confirmed from the county's pages. Still NO rate (the county posts none; call 641-856-8528). Fit unconfirmed (no lengths; sites under canopy, not visible on imagery). Ownership state -> local suggested (county conservation board runs it, as Swan Lake 3016); policy_ref none suggested. Not waterfront kept. Pin at the conservation office; campground not locatable. Note cleaned.
flags: OWNERSHIP (state -> local): the park is state-owned but run by Appanoose County Conservation, whose offices are in it ('It acts as headquarters to the Appanoose County Conservation offices'; the county lists it among 'ACCB Areas'). Ownership names who runs the campground; the curation doc files county-run campgrounds as `local`, and Swan Lake State Park (3016, Carroll County) is already `local` on the same footing. apply.py does not write ownership.

POLICY: the entry inherits the Iowa DNR row (state:IA), so the map shows a 14-night max and a booking note about ReserveAmerica's 10 pm cutoff that don't apply: the county takes no reservations ('Camping sites are issued on a first come first serve basis'). Suggest policy_ref none with the ownership change.

FEES: still no rate. Neither the mycountyparks park page nor the county's conservation page posts a camping fee, and the Camping activity page on mycountyparks returned an error page and stayed unread. The county office is (641) 856-8528 (also Google's phone). The sister park Lelah Bradley (3112, same board) is in the same state: p3-259 found no rate either.

FIT (keep with caveat): the county gives no pad lengths or rig limit; the six sites are in closed canopy on the bluff and can't be seen on NAIP or Esri imagery. No camper review read that states a rig length (The Dyrt's and Campendium's Sharon Bluffs pages 404; ParkAdvisor has one review). The proposed note says no lengths are given.

PIN: stored 40.72537,-92.80585 is the conservation office / nature center on 520th St (Google's park pin 40.725005,-92.804531 is ~100 m east). The campground can't be located under the canopy, so no corrected pin is offered.

WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. The Chariton River (~20-30 m wide, creek-class by width) runs along the park's east side ~350-450 m from the office, below the bluffs; the county puts the campground on the bluff top by the shelter. No sites visible on imagery, no official campsite photos. Distances are imagery estimates; Overpass was unavailable.
